context.body: A famous preserved household is invoked to make a point about the limit of another person’s righteousness.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: Across famine, animals, sword, and pestilence, Noah is named with Daniel and Job as a righteous person who could deliver only himself.
observations.label: Ezekiel limits what Noah’s righteousness can deliver: action

observations.body: Even sons and daughters would not be delivered by the presence of those righteous people in the judged land.
observations.label: Ezekiel limits what Noah’s righteousness can deliver: response

observations.body: Noah, Daniel, and Job · their righteousness · only their own souls
observations.label: Words in Ezekiel 14:12–20

payload.posture: Read Ezekiel 14:12–20 as ancestry and later memory evidence before carrying it into another source.
payload.tension: Ezekiel’s hypothetical claim stands beside Genesis’ household preservation without explaining the two settings as identical.
payload.title: Ezekiel limits what Noah’s righteousness can deliver
